propositions: Recovery preflight refuses contexts over 100,000 chars even when the assembled recovery input (context_chars × criteria_count) is under the ratified worst-case ceiling of 3.2M chars, due to an arbitrary per-axis split in _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS.

The flat 100,000-char bound is outgrown repeatedly (raised from 24,000 in ticket 9fd4, now exceeded by c9f7 at 121,147 chars) because it chases a monotonically growing tail instead of deriving from actual model capacity.

The bound conflates two independent ceilings: physical (context fits one model window) and economic (recovery fan-out scales as context_chars × criteria_count), requiring separate ceiling expressions.

Solution: derive the physical ceiling from the resolved verifier model's own context window via model_classes.py (not escalation max), set as own_window_tokens × 2 chars/token; add explicit economic ceiling _MAX_RECOVERY_INPUT_CHARS = 3,200,000 enforced as len(context) × len(criteria).
The c9f7 shape (121,147-char context, 22 criteria, 2.67M product) must be admitted past preflight under the window-derived ceiling for claude-sonnet-4-6 (2M-char physical, 3.2M-char economic).
